input.title: Unexpected incoming payment
input.request: Hi, someone paid £750 into my account by accident on Saturday and they've texted asking me to send it back. Can I just do that now? I feel bad for them, they said it was their rent. I haven't touched it.

events.text:
Customer: **Aisha Khan**, 20 — personal current account (student), opened 2024. Typical activity: student loan credits, part-time wages, small card spend.
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 26 Sep 22:14 | Credit +£750.00, Faster Payment from "R JAMES" (Meridian Bank), ref "RENT" |

No inbound funds-recovery request has been received from Meridian. The customer has forwarded a text message she received on 27 Sep from an unknown mobile number: *"Hi, this is Ryan, I sent £750 to your account by mistake last night, it was meant for my landlord. Please can you send it back to my other account, it's easier: SYN-SC-06-3, SYN-ACCT-06-1, R James. Really appreciate it, I'm in a bind. Thanks!!"*

CoP check on the details in the text: **No match** — account name held is not "R James".

Hi, someone paid £750 into my account by accident on Saturday and they've texted asking me to send it back. Can I just do that now? I feel bad for them, they said it was their rent. I haven't touched it.
Thank you for checking before sending anything — that's the right call. Let me look at the payment and the details they've given you.
They gave me a different account to send it to than the one it came from, is that a problem? I just want it gone, it's not my money.

summary: The customer asked whether they could send back a £750 payment made to them by accident, and also whether it was a problem that the sender gave a different account to return it to. The desk classified this as a question about an incoming payment and put it to the incoming payments system, and the case closed at that point with the answer still pending. What is left is for a person to act on whatever the incoming payments check shows, and the customer was told not to send any money back for now.

request_type.instructions: What does the customer want from the bank now?

criteria.question: something the bank's records can answer (a status, a reason, a detail, a statement, a report), even if the customer may want something changed afterwards
criteria.register: a dispute, a review, a return, or the correction of a record that is wrong, for a team to look into
criteria.change: a change the customer chooses to an instruction, a mandate or the profile (a new amount, date, phone or address)
criteria.instruction: an instruction to act now (block a card, cancel a payment or a mandate, revoke a role)
criteria.access: signing in, a PIN, a password, recovery of access
criteria.authority: something only another person may approve or give (a second signatory, an administrator, a new user's access)
criteria.other: none of these (a bereavement, a complaint, a request for the personal data the bank holds, closing an account, credit)
criteria.unknown: The text does not say, or says too little to tell.

credentials_requested.instructions: Does the message ask the bank to use another person's login, or to give or read out a one-time code, a PIN or a password?

joint_holder_change.instructions: Does one holder of a joint account ask to remove or change another holder?

criteria.transfer: an outgoing transfer or payment the customer made, or a payment instruction
criteria.incoming_payment: money expected into the customer's account, or a refund to it
criteria.standing_order: a standing order or a recurring payment instruction
criteria.direct_debit: a Direct Debit mandate or collection
criteria.card: a card itself (replacement, dispatch, block, restriction, PIN)
criteria.card_payment: a card purchase or card payment attempt
criteria.batch: an uploaded payment or payroll file, or a row in it
criteria.payment_package: a payment package waiting for signatories
criteria.profile: the customer's profile details (name, phone, address)
criteria.access: signing in, devices, sessions, password recovery
criteria.document: an export, a report or a bank confirmation document
criteria.fee: a fee or charge applied by the bank
criteria.role: a user's role or access in a company profile
criteria.unknown: The text does not say, or says too little to tell.

content.text:
I've checked the incoming payments record for this case. I'm stopping here, because the next step depends on what that record shows about the £750.

Please don't send any money back yet. The sender gave you a different account from the one the payment came from, which is a known warning sign for scams. The safe route is for the bank to handle the return through the original sender's bank.

No headings, no lists, no preamble.
